# NT OFFICIAL SAFETY MANUAL ## SECTOR APPALIA MAJORIS ## MEDICAL PROFESSIONAL EYES ONLY
In addition to the standard safety manual, Nanotrasen finds it prescient to inform you of these additional possible threats and how to react to them. The following list describes various afflictions and how to treat patients that may present with them.
## Romerol
Romerol is a synthetic reagent that causes mass reanimation of flesh in those afflicted. The symptoms typically present as psychosis, followed by an acute episode of violent behavior. Patients suffering from a romerol overdose should be sequestered and neutralized as soon as possible until a cure becomes available. The saliva and expiration from a romerol patient is likely to transmit infectious particulates to unaffected individuals.
Therapeutic methods for resolving a romerol overdose require the synthesis of ambuzol. This reagent has been shown to quickly expunge all traces of romerol from patients as well as reestablish standard cellular function. A bolus of 10 units ambuzol administered via syringe should be the standard response to any romerol overdose aboard your vessel.
The following list of reagents is intended for [color=#42636d][bold]Chemists[/bold][/color] who are tasked with reverting a romerol overdose.
## Letoferol
Letoferol, a stereoisomer of the aforementioned romerol, bears many of the same ill effects on patients. This includes reanimation of the flesh and bouts of violent behavior, but patients suffering from a letoferol overdose appear quite differently. Often these patients display elongated bone structure and violent muscular reformation that is considered far outside of normal ranges. Their bodies appear to be covered in flesh-like growth with unnatural skeletal protrusions visible in multiple locations.
Much like those suffering from a Romerol overdose, these patients are best treated firstly by sequestering and neutralizing those affected. Mesotaxinide applied topically dissolves the malformations present in affected patients, but care should be taken to not over-apply mesotaxinide once the patient is neutralized.
After the patient is neutralized, a bolus of 15 units mesotaxinide or 40 units mesophenerol should be administered as soon as is safely possible. Following this dose the patient is expected to return to their previously unaffected form.
The following list of reagents is intended for [color=#42636d][bold]Chemists[/bold][/color] who are tasked with reverting a letoferol overdose.
## Macroparasites
Macroparasitic infection is uncommon in this sector due to modern vaccination efforts. However, the steps to treat them are listed below.
### Cestoda horrida (or the “Head Slug”)
Though the likelihood of you encountering a head slug infection during your shift is low, you should still be aware of the signs and symptoms that are often expected in a patient suffering from a head slug.
Oftentimes the afflicted display adaptations and athletic abilities far outside the standard range for their respective demographic, such as the ability to recover from seemingly fatal circumstances. If by chance your department is delivered a partially dissolved, seemingly hollow corpse, you are advised to inform either the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Medical Officer[/bold][/color] or the nearest [color=#ba292c][bold]Security Officer[/bold][/color] of this discovery as soon as possible. Treatment requires brain transplantation, typically into a cloned body donor.
Beyond these adaptations and abilities, the best method for determining if your patient is suffering from a head slug infection is by taking a blood sample and allowing either a [color=#42636d][bold]Chemist[/bold][/color] or your [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Medical Officer[/bold][/color] to run the blood sample through a standard centrifugation cycle. A violent, exothermic reaction within the blood itself is considered a positive result.
Outside of testing those you may believe are afflicted, standard response to reported [italic]C. horrida[/italic] aboard your vessel is to ensure all morgues remain firmly shut to prevent posthumous infections.
### Corticalus solium
[italic]C. solium[/italic] is a macroparasite that resides in the cortical region of its host. Their lifecycle involves a multiphase maturation period within the host’s cortical region, before traveling to the stomach where parthenogenesis occurs. Symptoms of a [italic]C. solium[/italic] infection will typically present in a neurological fashion.
Treating [italic]C. solium[/italic] involves suppression by ingestion of sugar, then by surgical extraction from the brain.
### Others
There can exist a multitude of less documented forms of macroparasites that you or your coworkers may become exposed to. Should a patient present to your clinic complaining of pain in the lower abdomen as well as writhing under the skin, please locate the nearest surgeon to verify the existence of a parasitoid infection.
